text:
alex: Heads-up — running into inconsistent ESM/CJS resolution across bundlers when packaging the JS SDK for edge runtimes. Minimal repro below, wondering if anyone else sees different behaviour across vite/rollup/webpack.

maria: what versions and a minimal repro would help. bundle output or runtime error?

alex: node 18.18, vite 5.0.2, rollup 3.30, webpack 5.88. Repro steps (super minimal):

package.json:
```
{"name":"repro-sdk-bundle","type":"module","dependencies":{"redwood-inference":"0.12.0"}}
```

src/entry.ts:
```ts
import Redwood from 'redwood-inference';
console.log(Redwood.clientVersion);
```

vite.config.ts:
```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
export default defineConfig({
  build: { target: 'es2020' },
  optimizeDeps: { include: ['redwood-inference'] },
  ssr: { noExternal: ['redwood-inference'] }
});
```

Commands:
```
npm i
npm run build (vite)
node dist/entry.js
```

Runtime error (vite build + run in edge):
```
Uncaught ReferenceError: require is not defined
 at dist/entry.js:1:1234
```

maria: curious — does the package ship both cjs and esm? check package.json of redwood-inference for "exports" or "main"/"module" fields.

alex: it has: "main": "dist/index.cjs.js", "module": "dist/index.esm.js", plus an exports map. The issue looks different per bundler:
- vite + ssr.noExternal => bundles esm but at runtime errors about global `require` when used in edge shim
- rollup (app is using rollup config with commonjs plugin) => build fails: "'default' is not exported by node_modules/redwood-inference/dist/index.cjs.js"
- webpack => builds but in edge runtime: "ReferenceError: process is not defined" from a tiny helper in the cjs entry

jonathan: classic. two orthogonal problems: (1) packages that provide both cjs+esm but rely on small runtime helpers that assume node shims (process/fs), (2) bundlers picking the wrong entry due to exports conditions.

maria: quick checks: for vite the common fix is adding ssr.noExternal: ['redwood-inference'] (you already did) or force ESM with optimizeDeps.include — but that only helps dev server. For build you need to make sure the ESM entry is resolved by the export conditions. Can you paste the exports map?

alex: exports map excerpt: 
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js",
    "import": "./dist/index.esm.js"
  },
  "./node": {
    "require": "./dist/node.cjs.js",
    "import": "./dist/node.esm.js"
  }
}
```

sam: that explains it. Some bundlers (notably webpack <=5 without proper exports resolution flags) will pick the require path for compatibility. For edge runtimes you want the import path. Workarounds:
- force resolver to prefer "import" condition (in webpack, set `resolve.conditionNames = ['import', 'default']`)
- use `alias: { 'redwood-inference': 'redwood-inference/dist/index.esm.js' }`
- or publish a pure ESM entrypoint at the package root and set "type":"module" in the dist package (harder).

maria: on rollup side, if the package has a cjs file with `module.exports =` and you're doing `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'`, rollup + plugin-commonjs can mis-handle default interop. Try rollup plugin config: `commonjs({ requireReturnsDefault: "namespace" })` or `requireReturnsDefault: "auto"` depending on plugin version.

alex: tried `requireReturnsDefault: 'auto'` — still get `is not exported` for named imports used internally.

jonathan: also watch out for side-effect: the cjs build may reference `process.env.NODE_ENV` which turns into `process` at runtime. In edge runtimes there's no process. Solutions: polyfill (not ideal) or ensure bundler replaces `process.env` at build time (DefinePlugin for webpack or rollup-replace plugin).

ci-bot: CI failure (PR #1347): build:ci:bundle (webpack) — exit code 1. See https://ci.internal/reports/1347

maria: short-term repro fix that worked for me locally: alias to the ESM bundle + ts declaration hack. In vite config: 
```
resolve: {
  alias: {
    'redwood-inference$': 'node_modules/redwood-inference/dist/index.esm.js'
  }
},
ssr: {
  noExternal: [] // remove, so we force resolution to the aliased esm file
}
```

alex: that fixes runtime errors for vite but doesn't solve rollup/webpack CI. For webpack I had to set `resolve.fallback: { fs: false, path: false }` and add `new webpack.DefinePlugin({ 'process.env.NODE_ENV': JSON.stringify('production') })`. Ugly but it unblocks builds.

sam: for TS typing problems: many consumers see "Could not find a declaration file for module 'redwood-inference'" if they import the ESM `.js` directly. Two options: ship an `index.d.ts` at package root and point `types` to it, or add a lightweight `index.d.ts` that re-exports types from the built dts. As a temporary DX workaround, add `declare module 'redwood-inference';` in a `types/globals.d.ts` in the app.

alex: logged a tiny SDK change proposal: 1) add an `exports` condition for `import:development`/`import:production`? maybe overkill. 2) publish a thin `dist/esm-entry.mjs` that is pure ESM and doesn't reference node helpers. 3) include a `types/index.d.ts` at package root. Opened issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/298 and PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/299

maria: thanks. For reproducibility docs we should add a short "Bundler pitfalls" doc in devex: list of bundler-specific fixes (vite alias, rollup commonjs plugin flags, webpack resolve.conditionNames + DefinePlugin + fallbacks). Also add a minimal repro repo link to the issue.

jonathan: I'll add a checklist to the issue with the exact commands to reproduce (vite/rollup/webpack), the failing logs, and the minimal fix matrix. We should also add a CI job that runs the sample app with each bundler to avoid regressions.

alex: thanks all — PRs incoming. If anyone wants the tiny repro repo I pushed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-sdk-bundle (branch: alex/bundle-repro).
